chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, fasting is not merely abstaining from food and drink. Then he said: Maryam said, 'I have vowed a fast to the Beneficent,' i.e., a fast of silence. And in another copy: 'i.e., silence.' So when you fast, preserve your tongues, lower your gaze, do not dispute, and do not envy.

He said: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) heard a woman insulting her maid while she was fasting. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called for food and said to her, 'Eat.' She said, 'I am fasting.' He said, 'How can you be fasting when you have insulted your slave girl? Indeed, fasting is not merely from food and drink.'

He said: And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you fast, let your hearing and your sight fast from the prohibited and the ugly, leave off quarreling and hurting the servant, and let the dignity of fasting be upon you, and do not make the day of your fasting like the day of your breaking fast.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and ethical significance of fasting beyond abstaining from food and drink in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'sawm al-jawarih' (fasting of the limbs), asserting that physical abstinence is incomplete without sensory and ethical restraint, a principle rooted in the Shia tradition of holistic worship. By citing Maryam’s vow of silence and the Prophet’s rebuke of a woman insulting her maid, it highlights that verbal and visual sins invalidate the spiritual merit of the fast. The narration concludes with practical advice to maintain the solemnity of fasting throughout the day, ensuring one's conduct reflects the inner state of devotion.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Fasting is not from the food and the drink alone’.

Then said: ‘Maryamas said: [19:26] Surely I have vowed a fast to the Beneficent, i.e., a Fast of silence’. (And in another copy: ‘i.e., silence). Therefore, whenever you Fast, preserve your tongues, and lower your gaze, and neither dispute not envy’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> heard a woman insulting a maid of her and she was Fasting. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> called for the food and said to her: ‘Eat’. So she said, ‘I am Fasting’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘How can you happen to be Fasting and you have insulted your slave girl. The Fast is not from the food and the drink (only)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever you Fast, so let your hearing, and your vision Fast from the Prohibition and the ugliness, and leave the disputing and hurting the servant, and let the dignity of the Fast be upon you, and do not make the day of your Fasting to be like a day of your breaking (not Fasting)’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al- Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Mada’iniy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that fasting is not fasting from food and drink only.” He then said, “Mary had said, ‘I have made a vow (promise) before the Beneficent to fast,’ meaning not to speak to anyone and remain silent, according to another script. When you fast, you should control your tongue, cast down your eyes, you must not quarrel and you must not be jealous.”

The Imam then said, “The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once heard a woman abusing her fasting servant. The Messenger of Allah asked for food and then asked the woman to eat. She said, ’I am fasting.’ He then said, ‘How can you be fasting while speaking words of abuse against your housemaid? Fasting is not fasting from food and drink only.’”

He (the narrator) has said, that abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, “When you fast, your ears and eyes must also stop committing unlawful acts and evil matters. You must not quarrel or hurt your servant. You must maintain the dignity of fasting and you must not make your day of fasting just like another day.”
